output.summary: KEP-2200 proposed a built-in admission controller, "DenyServiceExternalIPs", that rejects CREATE or UPDATE operations adding new values to Service.spec.externalIPs, while tolerating and allowing removal of existing values. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: The KEP responds to CVE-2020-8554, where an unprivileged user can hijack an IP address through Service.spec.externalIPs. The design argues that type=LoadBalancer uses Service status, which most users should not be able to write, and that externalIPs has few remaining use cases. A built-in admission controller was chosen over a webhook because most users never use the feature and should not have to run a webhook to be protected.

alternatives.option: Force users to use policy controllers as webhooks
alternatives.why_not: The readme rejects this as burdensome: "making them ALL run a webhook seems terrible."

alternatives.option: Make a breaking API change and disable or rip-out the feature
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists making this the default (a breaking change) as a non-goal, so the feature is kept but blocked by an admission control flag.

alternatives.option: Add a new flag telling validation logic to disallow this field
alternatives.why_not: Listed under Alternatives in the readme; the source excerpt gives no explicit reason for rejecting it.

alternatives.option: Make a more complex API to define which namespaces or IPs may use this feature
alternatives.why_not: Listed under Alternatives in the readme; the source excerpt gives no explicit reason for rejecting it.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes to block the use of ExternalIPs via a built-in admission controller. The justification for this, as opposed to a webhook, is that 99% of users will never use this feature
This KEP proposes to add a built-in admission controller "DenyServiceExternalIPs", which rejects any CREATE or UPDATE operation which adds a new value to `Service.spec.externalIPs`.
Make it possible to disable an insecure feature for the vast majority of users very quickly.
In contrast, `type=LoadBalancer` uses Service status, which most normal users should not be allowed to write.
